taskDescription: Drag the correct conjugation reaction into each blank.
textField: The commonest Phase II reaction is *glucuronidation*, which uses UDP-glucuronic acid and is deficient in newborns and Gilbert syndrome; the conjugation that neutralises the toxic paracetamol metabolite NAPQI uses *glutathione* as its nucleophile; and the Phase II reaction whose genetic polymorphism classifies patients as slow or fast metabolisers is *acetylation*.

overallFeedback.feedback: Glucuronidation handles the largest share of conjugation and its neonatal deficiency explains physiological jaundice; glutathione conjugation is the critical defence against reactive electrophiles such as NAPQI; and acetylation polymorphism (NAT2) determines whether isoniazid and other drugs are cleared slowly or quickly, affecting both efficacy and toxicity.
